clue.text: Leading for a little time, among the trees

indicators.note: among says the short time sits between the letters of the trees

parts.note: a forest is a mass of trees
MO is short for moment, a little time

explanation.surface: Someone takes the lead briefly while walking in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts MO inside FOREST, after its first four letters; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost and leading are synonyms: both mean first in position or rank.

clue.text: Easy-going, yet has a row about a bill

indicators.note: about means the row goes round the bill, enclosing it

parts.note: a file is a row, as in single file
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A relaxed person still argues over the restaurant bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line, FILE; 'about' puts it round AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile can mean easy or effortless, close to easy-going in manner.

clue.text: Become amenable about a time of fasting

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone softens their stance around the season of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to give way and soften, becoming more agreeable.

clue.text: Large bird seen to attack this Old Testament character

parts.note: the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand
to bite is to attack with the teeth

explanation.surface: A giant bird is spotted pecking at a Biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moabite was a native of Moab, a people named in the Old Testament, such as Ruth.

clue.text: Running out of the cellar?

parts.note: the cellar is not a basement but a table container, and what runs out of it is the seasoning it holds

explanation.surface: Someone flees from the basement.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is poured, or runs, from a salt cellar at the table.

clue.text: It's rarely models change position

indicators.note: models changing position suggests these letters taking new places

explanation.surface: Fashion models only occasionally switch poses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change position' rearranges MODELS; 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom and rarely are synonyms meaning not often.

clue.text: Morally improved — may even be deified

indicators.note: may even be signals that the word deified could be turned into another arrangement of itself

explanation.surface: A person morally uplifted might go so far as to be made a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may even be' rearranges DEIFIED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edified means instructed and uplifted, improved in mind or morals.

clue.text: Depict Her Majesty cruelly, as old and enfeebled

indicators.note: a cruel depiction distorts its subject, so the letters are distorted

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A cartoonist portrays the Queen unkindly as frail and aged.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes someone worn out and weakened by age.

clue.text: Has possibility of containing awful din this time

indicators.note: containing means the possibility word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: might expresses possibility, as in it might rain

indicators.note: awful means the letters of din are mangled

explanation.surface: A dreadful racing noise may occur at this late hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns DIN into IDN, and 'containing' puts it inside MIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points to a particular hour; twelve at night is a time.

clue.text: Reprehensible to put plug back with tip missing, in wire

indicators.note: in means the shortened piece is set inside the wire

parts.note: a cable is a wire

indicators.note: the tip is the leading letter of the turned word, which goes
put back means the word plug is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone is to blame for fitting a plug the wrong way round onto a wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PLUG into GULP; 'with tip missing' drops G to leave ULP; 'in' puts it inside CABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Culpable means deserving blame, which is what reprehensible conveys.

clue.text: Ground dug up around reactor core

indicators.note: around means the dug word surrounds the central letter

parts.note: mined means dug from the earth

indicators.note: the core of a word is its centre letter

explanation.surface: Earth is excavated near a nuclear plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of REACTOR is C, and 'around' puts MINED round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground meat is minced meat: both mean chopped very small.

clue.text: A gear change secures Tourist Trophy, in this event

indicators.note: secures means the rearranged letters hold the trophy letters fast inside
a gear change suggests the letters of a gear shifting

parts.note: TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist shifts gear and wins the Isle of Man TT.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns A GEAR into REGAA; 'secures' puts TT inside it after REGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a boating event, a series of races on water.

clue.text: Pulse is fast at one-fifty

parts.note: Lent is the Christian fast
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A heart rate holds steady at one-fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is a seed of the pea family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes; the lentil is one example.

clue.text: Live Red Indian chiefs doubled up with this illness

indicators.note: doubled up means the whole piece built so far appears twice

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: chiefs are the leading letters of the words

explanation.surface: An old Western scene of two chiefs struck down by disease.
explanation.walkthrough: BE plus RI (the first letters of Red Indian) gives BERI, which 'doubled up' repeats.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by a lack of vitamin B1.

clue.text: Goggling up the creek, at sting — rays? Stay away!

indicators.note: up the creek means in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word stay is the set of letters taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: Wide-eyed in a creek at the sight of stingrays, a swimmer is warned off.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of AT STING RAYS, remove S, T, A, Y ('Stay away'), and 'up the creek' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Goggling and staring both mean looking wide-eyed.

clue.text: See me going for the vintage port — then the picnic fare

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'See me going for the vintage port — then the picnic fare (4,8)': SANDWICH is the port, but no reading of 'See me going for the vintage' gives MEAT; likely garbled in OCR, and no scan or web source gives the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: See me going for the vintage port — then the picnic fare

clue.text: Pretended to be deeply moved

definitions.meaning: faked or put on, as an assumed manner

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both feigned (an artificial accent) and emotionally stirred (moved by the news).

clue.text: A servant turns up in the hotel with this old vessel

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the hotel

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a maid is a female servant

explanation.surface: A maid appears at the hotel aboard an old ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses A MAID to DIAMA, and 'in' puts it inside INN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a large merchant sailing ship trading with India, such as an East Indiaman.

clue.text: Window arrangement requiring a new fastener on it

indicators.note: new suggests the letters being formed afresh

explanation.surface: Fitting a window needs a new catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges FASTENER plus ON IT; 'requiring a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenestration is the architectural term for the arrangement of windows in a building.

clue.text: Butterfly I'd seen on a goat-like creature

indicators.note: in a down clue, seen on means placed below the next piece

parts.note: a satyr is a woodland god, part man and part goat

explanation.surface: A butterfly is spotted alighting on a mythical goat-man.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrids are a family of brown butterflies, such as the meadow brown.

clue.text: Unconventional, though a former policeman?

definitions.meaning: an officer no longer patrolling the streets is off his round

explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unusual; a policeman off the beat is no longer on his patrol route.

clue.text: Many a girl's motive for gossip?

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Plenty of girls spread rumours for a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice, a wish to harm, is a common motive behind spiteful talk.

clue.text: Commercial airway coming

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a vent is a passage for air

explanation.surface: An advertisement for an airline is on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means arrival or coming, as in the advent of spring.

clue.text: Actual way out, holding machine-gun

indicators.note: holding means the way out contains the gun

parts.note: an exit is a way out
the Sten was a British light machine-gun

explanation.surface: A real escape route is guarded by a gunman.
explanation.definitionFit: Existent and actual both mean really there, in being.

clue.text: Why one is reluctant to make a force attack?

parts.note: F stands for force in physics
a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: A commander hesitates to order troops to raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Why one is' and 'to make' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being scared of something makes one unwilling, so fearful stands in for reluctant here.

clue.text: Take cover, having nothing on, in the swimming place

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: a lid is a cover
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Bathers go unclothed at the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having nothing on' looks like nudity, but O is placed under LID.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: Pitch from the wood, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals that the wood word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: timber is wood

explanation.surface: A note comes from the trees, judging by what one hears.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the tone quality of a sound, loosely its pitch or tone.

clue.text: He's enterprising — electrifying!

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a lively, energetic person and a conductor carrying electric current.

clue.text: Strip off in Dundee

indicators.note: off means the letters of the city are gone wrong

explanation.surface: People undress in a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges DUNDEE, a Scottish city; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to strip bare, as wind strips a hillside.

clue.text: Sole supporter

parts.note: sole is not only but the underside of a foot, and the support is something it rests on

explanation.definitionFit: A rest for the feet supports the soles.
